85.t: Max Roach in the big band
85.s: Roach's innovative drumming made it hard to find the one, and the band had to sneak back in after his solos.
85.q: Eventually it fit in, but it was very strange to me, because it was one of those, at the time he was so innovative that it was hard to know where one was, as I said before, you know. Let me know where one is, and I’ll find two on my own. But he had a tremendous technique then, you know, that has…

491.s: Golson describes Max Roach's place in bebop, his adventurousness and mustache, their one Riverside recording and his later ensembles M'Boom and the double quartet.
491.ch: Advice, education and the evolution of jazz
491.q: Max Roach. When Diz and Bird came on the scene, the drums, piano, and the bass were behind. They hadn’t caught up with them. They were playing stride and hi-hat, chik-ka-chih, Kaiser Marshall. One of the first drummers to get in tandem with them was Max Roach. And Curley Russell, yeah. I don’t…

328.s: Roach made drums a musical instrument.
328.q: Max was – I’m surprised that the other drummers didn’t hear what Max was doing, because he started making the drums a real musical instrument, especially when you played a solo. That solo had to be musical. You couldn’t just play the rudiments or play some fast rolls or something like that. You had…

371.t: Max Roach on 52nd Street compared with later drummers
371.s: Jones recalls Max Roach with Coleman Hawkins and the Parker-Gillespie group on 52nd Street and calls Roach compact where later drummers played more.
371.ch: The Great Jazz Trio, Goodman and Japan
371.q: There is a qualitative difference. For instance, you take Max Roach. I know you're familiar with his work. Max, when I first came to New York, was working on 52nd Street with Coleman Hawkins group. There was Charlie Parker with Dizzy Gillespie at the Three Deuces. That was a great crew with Bud…

64.t: Bebop's founders, the drummers and his Ellington-style voicings
64.s: Brown asks about ideas circulating among musicians; Taylor says the bebop founders were not drafted, traces drummers' roles, and defends the upper-register voicings he took from Ellington.
64.ch: New York scene and bebop community
64.q: But one of the things that was going on was the fact that the musicians basically who were conceptualizing bebop were not in the Army. Dizzy and Bird didn’t go in the Army. Bud was not in the Army. Kenny Clark did so he relinquished his part of that at that moment to Max Roach, until a later period…

166.t: Setting the record straight on Shelly Manne and a 'floating rhythm section'
166.s: He denies a floating rhythm section with Manne and Heywood; Manne, then in the Navy, learned by sitting in.
166.ch: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
166.q: Shelly Mann was in the Navy. He was stationed at Sheepshead Bay with Dick Stabile. Now he learned how to play drums but he didn't know anything about jazz. And Kenny Clark who they called Klook, just suffered a stroke recently in Paris which that broke up the Clarke Bold Band. I would ask -- Shelly…

117.t: Max Roach and Dave Tough on a cold Chicago street
117.s: Freeman recalls meeting Max Roach in the Chicago wind and talking for 35 minutes about Dave Tough, who he says influenced avant-garde drummers.
117.q: I remember running into Max Roach who we'd say is the father or grandfather, so-called of avant garde drumming and I don't, although Max himself wouldn't use that category, but that's what the critics called him.

168.t: Kenny Clarke's drumming and the shift to ride cymbal timekeeping
168.s: Stewart accepted Clarke's off-beat accents, and they agree the move from bass-drum quarter notes to ride cymbal let the bassist be heard, which suited Stewart for bebop.
168.q: It was a good sound, yeah, and he -- of course, at times, he played off tempos and what have you quite a bit. But I didn't -- that didn't bother me. I became used to that. Quite a few drummers, they were used to playing off-beat and what have you.

115.s: Dance and Gus list New York drummers: Specs Powell, Cozy Cole, Harold West, Max Roach and Kenny Clarke.
115.ch: Postwar: Chicago, Vinson, Hines and Cootie
115.q: Harold West, he was a good drummer. Everybody always used Harold West when I [came back.] Everybody was talking about Harold West.

103.t: Cliff Leeman, a Kansas City drummer who went to New York
103.s: Hinton begins a survey of drummers; Jones says Cliff Leeman knew Kansas City music but could not transplant it to New York bands.
103.q: Cliff Leeman came from Dan Murphy's Musical Skippers all the way from Portland, Oregon. Cliff Leeman quit the band in Kansas City and he was a sub-drummer with the jump-up band that Basie had. Nobody ever heard that band to speak of but people like - when Woody Herman came in with Isham Jones,…
